claims.claim: AI stories state their themes outright far more often than human stories (explicit narrator thematic commentary 77% vs 52%).

claims.claim: AI stories run one plot line with no subplots 79% of the time versus 57% for human stories.
AI stories express emotion through bodily-response description in 81% of stories versus 38% of human stories.
AI stories reach for smell imagery in 82% of stories versus 57% of human stories.
AI stories resolve through the protagonist's own action 69% of the time versus 46% for humans, and end ambiguously less often.
Human protagonists' choices are framed as morally ambiguous in 59% of stories versus 38% of AI stories.
claims.quote: frame protagonist' choices as more morally ambiguous

claims.claim: Human stories use chronological discontinuity, fourth-wall breaks (67% vs 39%), direct reader address (28% vs 7%) and named intertextual references (47% vs 24%) far more than AI stories.

claims.quote: occupy a rarer, more dispersed region of narrative space

claims.claim: Narrative-level features still identify AI fiction at 93.9% macro-F1 after professional-style rewriting, so surface edits do not humanize structure.
claims.quote: far harder to humanize

claims.claim: Each model family has a signature: Claude's event intensity escalates less, GPT over-uses gossip and dream sequences, Gemini writes the tidiest endings.

claims.claim: LLM-processed text shows abrupt excess of style words such as delves (28x), showcasing (10x), intricate, underscores, pivotal, meticulously, realm; 2024 excess words were 66% verbs and 16% adjectives.

claims.feature: lexical overuse not inherited from training data

claims.claim: LLM poems force closure with contrived mic-drop final lines.

claims.quote: contrived mic-drops like the last sentence

claims.claim: Negative parallelism in two shapes, 'not just X but Y' and 'not X but Y', is a catalogued sign of AI writing.
claims.source: Wikipedia editors, Signs of AI writing
claims.page: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: not a mirror but a portal: not representation, but mechanism

claims.claim: The construction fails cognitively: readers process the negated concept first and retain it, so the reframe lands weaker than the writer intends and compounds with repetition.
claims.page: Slanguage: Why AI's stylistic negation is both annoying and doesn't work
claims.quote: Your brain doesn't skip to the alternative.

claims.claim: In AI fiction the 'not X; Y' construction feels obligatory rather than natural, often alongside stacked triplets of descriptors.
claims.page: How to Identify AI-Written Web Fiction

claims.claim: The negation reframe borrows the sound of insight without delivering it.
claims.page: Don't Write Like AI (1 of 101): Negation
claims.quote: It tries to sound sophisticated without being sophisticated.

claims.claim: The 'isn't just X; it's Y' frame combined with a metaphor and a tricolon is a signature machine sentence that carries no content.
claims.page: Spotting machine-made prose
claims.quote: It says absolutely nothing at all.

claims.claim: AI narrators explicitly comment on the story's theme 77% of the time versus 52% for humans, with tighter thematic unity and more central moral questions.
claims.page: StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction
claims.quote: AI over-explains its themes

claims.claim: AI spells out meaning that human fiction leaves implied; the tell lives in the story's structure, not its word choice.
claims.page: The AI Tells Are in the Story
claims.quote: AI explains. Humans imply.

claims.claim: LLM verse refuses to state itself plainly yet re-restates its load-bearing moments, over-explaining what it has already shown.
claims.page: In Offense of LLM Poetry
claims.quote: Refusal to state itself too plainly, but tendency to re-restate

claims.claim: AI prose puts aphorisms where connective tissue should be and pivots to abstraction in place of concrete physical imagery.
claims.page: I Asked the Machine to Tell on Itself: A Field Guide to AI Tells

claims.claim: AI-assisted manuscripts carry heavy-handed thematic messaging that the editor had to strip back.
claims.page: After Editing Two AI-Assisted Manuscripts, I Rewrote My Client Agreement

claims.claim: AI fiction accumulates a recycled mood vocabulary drawn from Instagram-poetry registers, collapsing diverse tones into one.
claims.page: I Asked the Machine to Tell on Itself: A Field Guide to AI Tells
claims.quote: ache, hollow, tether, linger, fragile, fractured, ember, bloom

claims.claim: A cluster of grandeur nouns and verbs (testament, pivotal, delve, intricate, realm) co-occurs in LLM output and lends borrowed significance to flat subjects.
claims.source: Wikipedia editors, Signs of AI writing
claims.page: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: enduring testament to the influence of Italian colonial

claims.claim: Metaphors of symphonies, tapestries, and dances, plus delve/navigate/enhance/elevate, mark machine prose.
claims.page: Spotting machine-made prose
claims.quote: symphonies, tapestries, or complex dances

claims.claim: 'Quiet/magic' adverbs (quietly, deeply, fundamentally, remarkably) are used to make mundane description feel significant.
claims.page: Tropes - AI Writing Pattern Directory
claims.quote: Quietly orchestrating workflows and decisions

claims.claim: AI avoids plain copulatives, replacing 'is' with 'serves as' or 'holds the distinction of being'.
claims.source: Wikipedia editors, Signs of AI writing
claims.page: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: Harian Metro holds the distinction of being the first

claims.claim: AI metaphors are slightly off-target but stay in the right semantic neighborhood, and descriptions are mood-saturated pathetic fallacy such as rain mirroring grief.
claims.page: I Asked the Machine to Tell on Itself: A Field Guide to AI Tells

claims.claim: AI comparisons break when followed across a second dimension; the model does not grasp real-world metaphors or keep logical coherence.
claims.page: [Hot take] Problems with AI prose
claims.quote: AIs fail to grasp: real-world metaphors, logical coherence

claims.claim: AI stacks multiple comparisons onto one concept and overloads description with redundant sensory 'eyeball kicks'.
claims.page: How to Identify AI-Written Web Fiction

claims.claim: Forced figurative language sounds clever but obscures rather than clarifies.
claims.page: Tropes - AI Writing Pattern Directory
claims.quote: Like tracking weight loss on a rigged scale

claims.claim: AI carries emotion through bodily sensation and somatic metaphor 81% of the time versus 38% for humans, while naming emotions explicitly less often (8% vs 29%), an inversion of the usual 'AI tells emotions' assumption.
claims.page: StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction
claims.quote: AI overwhelmingly conveys emotion through physical sensations and bodily metaphors

claims.claim: AI narrators write as if no one is watching: fourth-wall breaks in 39% of AI stories versus 67% human, direct reader address 7% versus 28%.
claims.page: StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction
claims.quote: AI writes as though no one is watching

claims.claim: AI retreats from difficult material: it softens violence, obscures intimacy, and explains cruelty instead of rendering it.
claims.page: The Real Reason Not to Use AI to Write Your Novel
claims.quote: AI flinches every time

claims.claim: Language models optimize for predictability while good writing must surprise; AI output drifts rather than evolves with purpose.
claims.page: How to make AI write a bestseller—and why you can't
claims.quote: Good writing must be surprising. It needs to mix shit up.

claims.claim: Coherence begins to fall apart within a few hundred words, and when asked for a style the model over-applies it.
claims.page: How to make AI write a bestseller—and why you can't
claims.quote: It will often overdo the style you ask for

claims.claim: AI tools flatten authorial voice, homogenise, and eradicate creative risk-taking by applying blanket rules without understanding purpose.

claims.quote: They flatten voice and eradicate creative risk-taking.

claims.claim: The Granta AI story is lyrical nonsense with no narrative, reading like a parody of poet-turned-novelist fiction despite judges praising its 'lyrical precision'.

claims.quote: it does not have a story. There's no narrative.

claims.claim: Tricolon and stacked triplets of descriptors are overused as a default rhetorical shape.
claims.page: Tropes - AI Writing Pattern Directory
claims.quote: Products impress; platforms empower

claims.claim: AI keeps repeating a shape or cliché where even a bad human writer would notice and rest it, because its instinct is to keep obeying the instruction.

claims.quote: Even bad human writers give it a rest when noticing repetition

claims.claim: Em-dashes are overused, roughly one per paragraph, and used for thought continuation rather than breaks.

claims.quote: AI does this on a sentence level often with those em-dashes

claims.claim: AI holds an unnaturally locked point of view across scenes and paces every scene at the same rate.

claims.claim: Generated casts sound like one person and generated scenes run too long on screen, breaking pacing (vendor source with a stake in the fix).

claims.quote: A whole cast that sounds like one person

claims.claim: MFA readers strongly disfavored prompted AI pastiches on stylistic fidelity (OR 0.16), but after fine-tuning on the author's corpus both MFA and general readers preferred the AI, and it was flagged as AI only 3% of the time; the tells above characterize prompted default-register output.
claims.page: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers
claims.quote: Fine-tuned outputs were rarely flagged as AI-generated (3% vs. 97%)

claims.claim: 2,587 lay readers rated ChatGPT rewrites of three published short stories higher on quality and absorption than the originals and identified authorship at chance; the researchers attribute this to AI being clearer and more predictable, which is the same property editors name as the gloss.
